The latest Tracking SDG7 Progress Report reminds us that the global energy transition is not only a climate imperative but a development necessity.
 
Despite some progress, the world currently remains off track to meet #SDG7. As of 2023, 666 million people still lack access to electricity, and 2.1 billion rely on polluting fuels for cooking. These numbers are not just statistics: they represent lost opportunities for health, education, productivity and dignity. They provide us with both a reality check and a roadmap forward - which is where our focus must be:
 
🔋 Decentralized renewable energy (DRE) is already delivering results:
Between 2020 and 2022, DRE solutions accounted for +50% of new electricity connections in Sub-Saharan Africa. These technologies are affordable, resilient and ready to scale. With the right policy frameworks and investment flows, they can close the access gap in rural and underserved communities fast.
 
💰 Clean energy finance is growing - but it must be better targeted:
Global public finance for clean energy reached $21.6 billion in 2023, even amid economic and geopolitical instability. While incredibly promising, <10% reached EMDEs (excluding China). We need more concessional capital, blended finance models and de-risking tools to drive equitable investment where it’s needed most.
 
🍳 Clean cooking is rising on the agenda - and rightly so:
With only 7% of rural populations in Sub-Saharan Africa accessing clean fuels, now is the time to prioritize solutions that reduce health risks, empower women and support climate goals. Targeted investments in innovation and affordability can shift millions toward safer cooking practices.
 
At @UNDP, we see energy as a catalyst. Our integrated approach to sustainable energy is about more than about powering homes; it’s about unlocking futures. It’s about delivering health systems, schools, jobs, clean air, gender equality and climate resilience.
 
When we invest in energy for development, we multiply impact across the SDGs. What’s missing isn’t technology or resources: it’s urgency  and the willingness to act.  If we rise to the challenge and prioritize a just and inclusive energy transition, we can shape a future for people and planet where no one is left behind.
